caution: A failure to reproduce is not a finding that the paper is wrong. It may be a failure of the attempt.

attempts.label: CRCNS:fcx-3
attempts.entry_title: Frontoparietal working memory iEEG (Johnson et al. 2019) from CRCNS fcx-3
attempts.summary: In this intracranial dataset the paper's behavioural results held up: identity trials were slower than spatial and temporal ones, and accuracy did not differ by condition. Its per-subject power differences after the test cue held in part, with similar subject counts but smaller shares of electrodes, and sat at low frequencies. The frontoparietal phase-slope findings did not reproduce: with the null the Methods describe, 78 of 1135 pairs were directional in delta-theta, about what trial-shuffled data give, and the paper's counts appear only with the deposited code's null, which flags shuffled data as well. The absence of ERP differences failed in one subject, under a neighbour rule the paper does not state.
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Johnson, King-Stephens, Weber, Laxer, Lin and Knight (2019) on CRCNS data set fcx-3, which holds intracranial recordings from prefrontal and parietal cortex of 7 patients doing a visuospatial working memory task. It checks the channel and trial counts, the behaviour, ERPs and power between identity, spatial and temporal trials with per-subject cluster tests, and the phase slope index between prefrontal and parietal channels over the delay and in time.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Johnson et al. (2019) from CRCNS fcx-3

outcomes.notes: The data set's list of analysed channels (docs/summary_channel_analysis.csv) holds 187 channels, not 192. S4 has 5 right parietal channels where Table 1 gives 10; every other subject's PFC and parietal counts and hemispheres equal Table 1. PFC counts per subject are 4 to 54 (mean 19.00) and parietal 2 to 16 (mean 7.71). The list gives 1135 same-hemisphere PFC-parietal pairs, 6 more than 1129 (+0.5%); with 10 parietal channels in S4 it would give 1165, so neither count yields 1129. The totals differ by less than 10% (channels -2.6%), the criterion's partial match.
deviations: Counted from the data set's channel list, which every analysis here uses; all listed channels are present in the derived epochs.

outcomes.notes: Correct trials kept average 95.71 per subject; identity 32.14 +- 3.13 (26 to 35), spatial 32.86 +- 4.30 (27 to 39), temporal 30.71 +- 6.47 (20 to 39). Incorrect trials kept (reading (b)) average 17.29 +- 8.44 (4 to 25), the paper's values. Incorrect trials of all 120 (reading (a), from the per-subject accuracy of docs/summary_file.csv) average 18.29 with range 6 to 29, outside the widened range, so (b) is the matching reading and its mean is recorded. In S1 to S5 every correct trial of the 120 was kept.
deviations: Correct trials are those of the derived epochs with accuracy 1, the selection of the deposited scripts (power_compute.m, erp_compute.m).

outcomes.notes: Under reading (b), per subject and condition, accuracy runs from 0.625 to 0.975; under reading (a), per subject over conditions, from 0.758 to 0.950, whose lowest value is outside 0.63 +- 0.063. All values lie inside the widened range under both readings. The logit mixed model on all 120 trials finds no effect of condition (likelihood ratio p = 0.283 with condition as one term, p = 0.160 as two terms; kept trials p = 0.276). The paper reports p > 0.50; the p here is lower but above 0.05.
deviations: Accuracy over all 120 trials comes from docs/summary_file.csv (per subject and condition, over all trials by the data description), rebuilt as counts out of 40 per condition (Methods, "120 trials divided evenly"); the trial tables of S6 and S7 list only the kept trials.

The logit mixed model is fitted by maximum likelihood with Gauss-Hermite quadrature in Python; the paper names the model, not the software. Condition enters as one numeric term (the single degree of freedom of the paper's F(1,19)), with two dummy terms as a variant.

outcomes.notes: On subject-condition mean RTs (reading (a)), condition affects RT (F(1,19) = 6.04, p = 0.024); identity RT is longer than spatial (by 513 ms, F(1,12) = 11.81, p = 0.005) and temporal (by 392 ms, F(1,12) = 9.39, p = 0.010); spatial and temporal do not differ (p = 0.254). Identity RT is the longest in all 7 subjects. The F values are below the paper's bounds (F > 6.50, > 13.78, > 10.95) and the d values (1.30 and 1.16, mean paired difference over its SD) below its 2.14 and 1.91. Single kept correct trials (reading (b)) give p = 0.018, 0.037, 0.004 and 0.844.
deviations: Mean correct RT per subject and condition from docs/summary_file.csv (all correct trials, by the data description). Reading (b) uses the kept trials only, as the trial tables of S6 and S7 hold no others.
The paper does not say how Cohen's d was computed; d is reported, not judged.

outcomes.notes: Under the Methods' reading (segments zero padded, 30-Hz low-pass), neighbours adjacent by contact number and clusters judged at 0.05 per tail, S2 has a significant cluster for identity against temporal (p = 0.041); no other subject-contrast is below 0.05, and 2 of 14 have p <= 0.10 (paper, all p > 0.10). At 0.025 per tail the adjacent reading finds none, which would be reproduced; the distance reading (S5, p = 0.014) and no spatial clustering (S2, p = 0.024) find one at either threshold. Variants with adjacent neighbours at 0.05 per tail give, with the 1-30 Hz band-pass of the Results, no cluster (smallest p 0.085); per-trial baseline, S5 p = 0.030; the whole epoch filtered (erp_compute.m), S2 p = 0.031 (0.053 in round 1 with another random seed); 900-ms-delay trials only, S5 p = 0.023. Under the adopted reading the deciding p (0.041) is close to 0.05, where the Monte Carlo standard error of 1000 shuffles is about 0.006; the distance reading's p = 0.014 is about 6 standard errors below 0.05. The neighbour rule and alpha per tail are put to the paper's authors (findings).
deviations: Assumption. The paper says only that clusters were formed over "neighboring electrodes", and the deposited scripts hold no cluster test. The readings give different outcomes, so neighbours adjacent by contact number on the same lead or strip are adopted. This uses only the channel labels and follows the bipolar montage, which re-references each electrode "to the next adjacent electrode" (Methods, Data Acquisition and Preprocessing); the distance reading rests on placing numbered contacts on the grids of the MNI files, whose numbering the files do not document.

Clusters are judged at 0.05 per tail (the Methods' "fewer than 5% of randomizations yielded a larger effect", and FieldTrip's behaviour when cfg.alpha is 0.05 and the tails are not corrected); 0.025 is shown as a variant.

The 200-ms baseline and 900-ms processing segments are cut, zero padded to 7.5 s and low-passed (Methods, Event-Related Potentials, paragraph 1, "The correct-trial 200-ms pretrial baseline and 900-ms post-cue processing data segments were zero-padded to 7,500 ms ... and passed through a 30-Hz low-pass finite impulse response filter"). erp_compute.m filters the whole epoch and cuts the windows afterwards; where the Methods and the code differ the Methods come first (protocol, Reader step 2), and the code's order is a variant. The baseline is the pretrial temporal mean averaged over trials, one value per channel, as erp_compute.m computes it; it cannot change a t-test, so a per-trial baseline is run as a variant. The Results' "1-30 Hz bandpass" is a variant. The FIR order 3*fix(fs/30) (3*fix(fs/1) for the band-pass), forwards and backwards, is FieldTrip's default, implemented in scipy (a standard choice). FieldTrip itself was not run.

outcomes.notes: With the segment zero padded (Methods), adjacent neighbours, 0.05 per tail and assignment (a), 5 subjects show spatial > identity effects (S2 to S6) and 1 identity > spatial (S4; paper 2); the percentages of electrodes are 37.7 +- 21.1% and 11.8% (paper 54 +- 22% and 36 +- 12%). Under the main spectra, five subjects show spatial > identity effects under every neighbour reading and threshold, and S4 alone identity > spatial under each of them but adjacent neighbours at 0.025 per tail (none). The counts match within one subject and 5 of 7 subjects have a significant cluster, the criterion's partial match. The paper's counts (5 and 2, S7 added) appear only with the whole-epoch windows of power_compute.m (round 1's analysis), where the distance reading gives 52.0% (within tolerance) and 28.4% (outside). The significant clusters have p <= 0.028 (paper, all p < 0.04). On the 900-ms-delay trials alone 2 or 3 subjects show spatial > identity effects and none identity > spatial. A random draw of as many trials per condition from both delays gives 1 to 3 and 0 or 1, so that loss comes from the smaller number of trials, and these tests cannot show whether the 1150-ms trials' timing matters.
deviations: Power with 3-cycle Hanning windows, 2 to 40 Hz, 10-ms steps (power_compute.m), on the 900-ms processing segment embedded in zeros, every window computed (Methods, Spectral Decomposition, "Data segments were zero-padded to 7,500 ms"; S1 reading (a)). power_compute.m computes the windows over the whole derived epoch and cuts [0.3 1.2] s afterwards, so that windows longer than the segment take in the cue and the response period; that is shown as a variant, the Methods coming first. Computed in numpy.

The baseline z-score of zbaseline.m (r = all correct trials) is computed in closed form, the limit of its 1000 draws; it is the same affine map for every trial at a channel and frequency, so it cannot change the condition t-tests.
Neighbour rule and threshold as in erp-no-condition-difference; every reading is shown, with the per-subject percentages under each.

outcomes.notes: With the segment zero padded, adjacent neighbours, 0.05 per tail and assignment (a), 5 subjects show temporal > identity effects (paper 4) and 2 identity > temporal (S1, S7; paper 2), with 37.4 +- 20.5% and 21.0 +- 17.4% of electrodes (paper 68 +- 30% and 37 +- 10%). Assignment (b) gives the paper's counts, 4 and 2, with 41.2% and 21.0%. No reading brings both percentages within tolerance (distance reading, 47.8 to 55.2% for temporal > identity). The significant clusters of the effects counted have p <= 0.014 with adjacent neighbours; S2's temporal > identity cluster is significant only under the distance reading (p = 0.020) or without spatial clustering (p = 0.044). On the 900-ms-delay trials alone 1 to 3 subjects show temporal > identity effects and 1 (S1) identity > temporal; a random draw of as many trials from both delays gives 2 or 3 and 0 or 1.
deviations: As fig2-spatial-power.

outcomes.notes: With the segment zero padded, the subjects with identity > spatial or temporal effects are S1, S4 and S7 under every neighbour reading at 0.05 per tail. Under reading (b), identity against the mean of spatial and temporal, each has longer identity RT and lower identity accuracy, and the same holds under every other configuration printed (whole-epoch windows, 0.025 per tail, 900-ms-delay trials); under reading (a) S1 fails for the temporal contrast, where its identity and temporal accuracy are equal (0.825). S3 also has both without an identity > effect, so reading (ii) does not hold. Identity RT is the longest in all 7 subjects, so only accuracy separates subjects. The subjects come from the power claims, which are partially reproduced.
deviations: Accuracy (all 120 trials) and RT from docs/summary_file.csv.

outcomes.notes: With the segment zero padded and the density over all points (reading (b)), every neighbour reading meets the rule. With adjacent neighbours each effect is larger over 2 to 24 Hz than over 25 to 40 Hz (0.099 against 0.021, 0.097 against 0.032, 0.057 against 0.018) and has local maxima in 2 to 7 Hz (2, 3 and 2 Hz) and in 9 to 24 Hz. Without counting the 2-Hz end of the range as a maximum, the identity > other density (maxima at 2 and 14 Hz) has none in 2 to 7 Hz in any combination with reading (b), which would be the partial match. Over masked points only (reading (a)) the identity > other density is larger above 24 Hz under every combination. With the whole-epoch windows only the distance reading meets the rule.
deviations: Assumption. A point at either end of the 2 to 40 Hz range counts as a local maximum when it exceeds its one neighbour, the usual definition of a local maximum on a closed range; the claims file's rule does not say how the ends are treated, and the outcome depends on it (partial without it).

outcomes.notes: With the Methods' null, no subject's mean maintenance PSI z is below -1.96 under any reading. Reading (a), adopted, gives subject means -0.39 to 0.15 (delta-theta, mean -0.08 +- 0.20, recorded) and -0.67 to 0.04 (alpha-beta, -0.24 +- 0.25); reading (b) -0.67 to 0.05 and -0.48 to -0.05; with one permutation per trial the lowest subject mean is -1.27. The paper reports -40.03 +- 8.73 and -30.37 +- 2.60. Against psianalysis.m's null, reading (b) gives 4 of 7 subjects below -1.96 in delta-theta and none in alpha-beta, but that null gives |z| > 1.96 in 90 to 92% of trial-shuffled pairs. The deposited code without the conjugate gives every subject below -1.96 with the parietal channel first (means -55.47 and -69.83) and above +1.96 with the PFC channel first (+58.67 and +69.48); it is not a reading of the paper.
deviations: P1 details taken from psi_compute.m and subtracterp.m, ERP removed as the mean over all correct trials ("raw trial-wise mean", reading (a)); one Hanning-tapered FFT of each 900-ms segment padded to 7.5 s, read at the nearest bins to the integer frequencies ('mtmfft', spectra reading (a)); one PSI per band summed over adjacent bins.

The null follows the Methods (Task-Induced PSI, paragraph 2), "we randomly shuffled the frequencies in one signal and re-computed PSI 1,000 times". Each shuffle permutes the parietal spectrum's bins and recomputes the statistic that is z-scored, with the same permutation for every trial (null reading (a)) or one per trial (null reading (b)), both run. psianalysis.m z-scores the mean of per-trial PSI against the slope of the trial-mean spectrum with both factors shuffled, a different statistic; where the Methods and the code differ the Methods come first, and the code's null is a variant.

Assumption, for the PSI claims whose outcome depends on it (fig4c-alpha-beta-shift, fig5a-spatiotemporal-bidirectional, fig5b-alpha-beta-no-sustained). P1 leaves open whether PSI comes from trial-averaged cross-spectra (a) or per trial (b). Reading (a) with null reading (a) is adopted, since it is the first P1 lists, the measure of Nolte et al. (2008), and the only one whose z is calibrated. On trial-shuffled data its z has mean -0.05 and 0.02, SD 1.01 and 1.04, and |z| > 1.96 in 6.0% and 6.9% of pairs; reading (b) has mean -0.29 and SD 0.60 in delta-theta (0.1% pass), subject means from -1.25 to 0.52 in alpha-beta, and on synthetic independent signals a mean of -0.21 to -0.37, which one permutation per trial does not remove. The first revision adopted reading (b), for the structure of psianalysis.m and the Figure 4A legend's values "per subject across all trials"; round 2 of the verification found it uncalibrated. Here both readings give the same outcome.

outcomes.notes: No subject has net processing delta-theta PSI z above 0 under any reading (means -0.17 +- 0.16 under (a), adopted and recorded, -0.43 +- 0.34 under (b), and -0.21 and -0.76 with one permutation per trial; paper 6 subjects, 6.01 +- 6.42). Processing exceeds maintenance in the pair-level model under reading (b) (by 0.27, F(1,2268) = 114.2, p = 4.9e-26; paper F = 1936.10) but not under (a) (0.06, F = 2.2, p = 0.14); on subject means neither differs (paired t(6) p = 0.95 and 0.43). The partial match needs at least 4 subjects above 0. Against psianalysis.m's null, reading (b) gives 4 subjects above 0 and F = 58.5, but that null is not calibrated (90% of trial-shuffled pairs pass |z| > 1.96). On the 900-ms-delay trials alone 2 (a) or 1 (b) subjects are above 0.
deviations: As fig4-maintenance-parietal-led. The mixed model is computed as the paired test over pairs, which equals it when each pair has both intervals (checked against statsmodels MixedLM, F 2.2 against 2.2 under reading (a) and 116.4 against 114.2 under reading (b)). Degrees of freedom 2268 follow from 1135 pairs; as in the paper's degrees of freedom, pairs that share electrodes are treated as independent, which inflates F, so a paired t-test on subject means is printed beside it.

outcomes.notes: Under PSI reading (a), adopted because its z is calibrated, 5 of 7 subjects have processing alpha-beta PSI z below 0 (mean -0.14 +- 0.26, recorded; paper -12.60 +- 7.51), fewer than the 6 the partial match needs; one permutation per trial also gives 5. Processing is higher than maintenance by 0.11 in the pair-level model (F = 6.7, recorded, p = 0.0097; paper F = 2302.30). Under reading (b), 6 of 7 subjects are below 0 (S3 is above, 0.46; mean -0.57 +- 0.59) and processing exceeds maintenance by 0.43 (F(1,2268) = 97.9, p = 1.2e-22), but that reading's trial-shuffled surrogate gives nearly the same subject means (-1.17, -0.40, 0.52, -0.55, -0.60, -1.25 and 0.03, against the observed -1.07, -0.51, 0.46, -0.61, -0.72, -1.35 and -0.18; observed minus surrogate -0.08 +- 0.09, paired t(6) p = 0.061), and on synthetic independent signals its mean z is -0.25 to -0.29 in alpha-beta, so its 6 of 7 comes from its null. Under reading (a) observed minus surrogate is -0.01 +- 0.23 (p = 0.93). On subject means the interval difference is not significant under either reading (paired t(6) p = 0.48 under (a), 0.27 under (b)). Round 2 reviewed partially reproduced under reading (b); the change to not reproduced was proposed and round 3 agreed.
deviations: As fig4a-delta-theta-shift. The outcome rests on PSI reading (a) (see fig4-maintenance-parietal-led).

outcomes.notes: With the Methods' null, 78 (reading (a), adopted and recorded) or 1 (reading (b)) of 1135 pairs have processing |z| > 1.96 in delta-theta, and 104 or 74 in alpha-beta, against 1008 and 984. The trial-shuffled surrogate gives 68 and 78 under (a) and 1 and 71 under (b), and a null at 5% gives about 57, so the counts are near what signals without trial-locked coupling give. With one permutation per trial the counts are 98 and 93 (a) and 78 and 211 (b), against 75 and 71, and 76 and 194, on the surrogate. Against psianalysis.m's null, reading (b) gives 1014 and 1041, within tolerance (round 1's result), but the trial-shuffled surrogate gives 1022 and 1044 under the same null, so that count does not reflect directionality. The deposited code as written marks 1129 to 1135 of the 1135 pairs.
deviations: As fig4-maintenance-parietal-led; 1135 pairs, not 1129 (table1-electrodes).

outcomes.notes: No delta-theta time point differs between conditions after FDR under either PSI reading, with the segment zero padded or with the whole-epoch windows of psi_compute.m, in the pair-level model or in a paired test on subject means, so there is no sustained epoch. Reading (a), adopted, selects 78 directional pairs in 7 subjects; reading (b) selects 1 pair (S1).
deviations: Time-resolved PSI per psi_compute.m ('mtmconvol', per-condition ERP removed by subtracterp.m with three conditions), on the 900-ms segment zero padded (Methods, Time-Resolved PSI, "Spectral decomposition, PSI computation, and per-subject statistical bootstrapping analysis were otherwise identical"); psi_compute.m's windows over the whole epoch are a variant. The null is the Methods' frequency shuffle of one signal, recomputed per time point. subtracterp.m selects temporal trials by trialinfo column 5 (the delay), which selects none; the condition column is used.

The per-time-point mixed model is computed as the paired test over pairs (checked against statsmodels at three time points); FDR is Benjamini-Hochberg over the 91 points; a run is sustained when it spans at least 100 ms (P2), and runs over 100 ms are printed for the Figure 5 legend's ">100 ms" (asked of a reader). A paired t-test on subject means at each time point is printed beside it, since the model treats pairs that share electrodes as independent.

outcomes.notes: In the paper's four epochs no reading meets the criterion. Under reading (a), adopted (78 pairs), with the segment zero padded, the identity-trial grand means are 0.73, 0.60, 0.22 and -0.13 (recorded; paper > 2.62, > 2.35, < -3.04, < -3.57). Under reading (b) (S1's one pair) they are 1.31, 0.93, -1.98 and 0.13; the third passes -1.96 with the right sign (-2.20 as identity minus spatial) but is outside the bound (-3.04, within 10%). Every value of the other readings (averaging, measure, PSI and spectra) is below 1.96 in absolute value.
deviations: As fig5a-delta-theta-epochs; the paper's epochs are used.

outcomes.notes: Under PSI reading (a), adopted (78 pairs in 7 subjects), the spatial-trial and temporal-trial grand means stay at or below 0.87 and 1.01, under 1.96 at every one of the 91 time points and under the paper's 1.60, which the criterion counts as reproduced. The match shows little. Under this reading the identity-trial grand mean also stays below 0.99, where the paper reports |z| above 2.35, and the 78 pairs are about as many as the trial-shuffled data select (68). With the whole-epoch windows, reading (a) gives 0.37 and 0.56. Under reading (b) the selection leaves one directional pair (S1); its spatial-trial z reaches |z| = 3.07 (140 ms) and its temporal-trial z 2.36 (180 ms), with 16 and 11 points at |z| >= 1.96 (whole-epoch windows, 2.54 and 3.03), but its identity-trial z also passes 1.96 at 9 points, so on one pair such excursions are common. Round 2 reviewed not reproduced under reading (b); the change to reproduced was proposed and round 3 agreed.
deviations: The outcome rests on PSI reading (a) (see fig4-maintenance-parietal-led). As fig5a-delta-theta-epochs otherwise.

outcomes.notes: Under PSI reading (a), adopted (104 pairs in 7 subjects), no time point differs between conditions after FDR in the pair-level model (smallest p 0.0015 against spatial, 0.0027 against temporal), in the whole-epoch variant or in a paired test on subject means (0.016 and 0.024), which the criterion counts as partially reproduced. Under reading (b) (74 pairs in 6 subjects), 30 (identity against spatial) and 35 (against temporal) of 91 time points differ after FDR in the pair-level model (whole-epoch windows, 36 and 37), but the trial-shuffled data select 71 pairs under the same reading, S3 supplies 44 of the 74, and a paired test on the 6 subjects' means finds no point after FDR (smallest p 0.0029 and 0.0078). No reading shows a sustained run (longest 40 to 50 ms). Round 2 reviewed reproduced under reading (b); the change to partially reproduced was proposed and round 3 agreed.
deviations: The outcome rests on PSI reading (a) (see fig4-maintenance-parietal-led). As fig5a-delta-theta-epochs otherwise.

findings.statement: The data set's list of analysed channels (docs/summary_channel_analysis.csv) holds 187 channels where the paper reports 192 (Table 1). S4 has 5 right parietal channels (RLD6 to RLD8, RC10, RC11) where Table 1 gives 10. The list yields 1135 same-hemisphere PFC-parietal pairs, where the paper reports 1129; Table 1's counts would give 1165.

The description says summary_file_trial.csv holds information about each trial, with 120 trials per subject. In S6 and S7 it holds only the trials kept after artifact rejection (101 and 90 rows, numbered up to 120), matching their derived epochs; in S1 to S5 it holds all 120. Single-trial accuracy over all 120 trials cannot be rebuilt for S6 and S7 (summary_file.csv gives it per condition).

A timing contrast between trials with 900-ms and 1150-ms delays (70-150 Hz amplitude) shows, in S2, S3 and S4, responses in the processing epoch of the 1150-ms trials 0.21 to 0.26 s later relative to the trial table's processing column than in the 900-ms trials, and in S4 the same shift in the encoding epoch, while the pretrial epochs show shifts of 0.03 s or less. This is consistent with the encoding and processing columns (computed at fixed offsets from the pretrial start) lying about 0.25 s before the events in 1150-ms trials, which would put the end of the cue in their processing window. The test is weak in the other subjects (S1, S5 and S6 show shifts of 0.28 to 0.35 s in the processing epoch that do not pass the shuffle test) and does not prove it. The ERP and power tests and the task-induced PSI on the 900-ms-delay trials alone are shown as variants. Power on those trials loses most effects, and so does power on a random draw of as many trials from both delays, so these tests cannot tell whether the timing affects the results.

The deposited psianalysis.m computes the cross-spectrum as the product of the two channels' Fourier coefficients without the conjugate, unlike the cross-spectral density of the Methods and of Nolte et al. (2008). The resulting normalised spectrum depends essentially on one channel's phase (it equals plus or minus exp(2i x the phase of the second channel)), and the PSI z it gives is not antisymmetric; on these data it is +58.67 (delta-theta maintenance, mean over subjects) with the PFC channel first and -55.47 (sign reversed) with the parietal channel first. Its null is also not the statistic it z-scores. It averages per-trial PSI and compares the average with the slope of the trial-mean normalised spectrum, frequency-shuffled with both factors permuted independently, whose spread shrinks with the number of trials. The Methods say the frequencies of one signal were shuffled and PSI recomputed. Even with the conjugate added, this null gives |z| > 1.96 in 90% (delta-theta) and 92% (alpha-beta) of pairs when each subject's PFC and parietal trials are shuffled against each other, where a calibrated z gives about 5%.

The deposited psi_compute.m does not run as written. It uses an undefined `freq` (the signature takes subid and elecs only), saves to an undefined `savDir`, and tests the electrode argument with `nargin > 2`. Its subfunction subtracterp.m selects temporal trials with `trialinfo(:,5)==2`, the delay column, which selects no trial.

S7's derived epochs record a continuous recording of 431506 samples (hdr.nSamples) while the deposited data_primary.mat of S7 has 445952; the derived traces still match the deposited continuous data at the trial table's samples (r >= 0.9989). S3's elec_labels.mat is a MATLAB 5 file, the others MATLAB 7.3.

The electrode position files (s<n>_MNI_grid.csv) name grids and list positions in order, but do not say how the contact numbers of the channel labels map to grid positions, and S3's labels (RH1 to RH256) do not match the name of its grid (HD_Grid). The derived channels are bipolar, labelled by one contact, with the reference contact found here only from the data (the next contact on strips and depth leads, the next grid row on S3's and S6's grids).

Question for the paper's authors. Which electrodes were neighbours in the per-subject cluster tests (Methods, Event-Related Potentials, "neighboring electrodes"), and were clusters of each sign judged at 0.05 or 0.025? The deposited scripts hold no cluster test. The outcome of the ERP test depends on it here (adjacent contacts, S2 p = 0.041, significant at 0.05 per tail and not at 0.025; positions within 1.5 contact spacings, S5 p = 0.014). This attempt assumed contacts adjacent on the same lead and 0.05 per tail.

Question for the paper's authors. Was task-induced and time-resolved PSI computed from cross-spectra averaged over trials (Nolte et al. 2008) or per trial and averaged, as psianalysis.m does, and with which channel first, given that the deposited code omits the conjugate? And was the null the frequency shuffle of one signal with PSI recomputed, as the Methods say, or the slope of the trial-mean spectrum, as psianalysis.m computes it? With the Methods' null, 1 (per trial) or 78 (trial-averaged) of 1135 pairs are directional in delta-theta, and 74 or 104 in alpha-beta, near the counts of trial-shuffled data; the paper reports 1008 and 984, which only the code's null reproduces (1014 and 1041), and that null gives about the same counts on trial-shuffled data. This attempt used the Methods' null and adopted the trial-averaged reading, whose z is calibrated on trial-shuffled data, where the readings give different outcomes; per-trial PSI with the Methods' null gives z offset from zero on data without coupling.

verifications.by: Independent agent run by CatalystNeuro (same harness, separate context, did not write the notebook)
verifications.reviewed: Round 1. The first executed notebook with the conclusion cells and the summary removed, the helper module and the claims file, with the paper. Its report gave its own outcome for each claim; all 17 agree with the record as it then stood. It listed 10 problems, 5 marked as affecting a conclusion.

verifications.by: Independent agent run by CatalystNeuro (same harness, separate context, did not write the notebook)
verifications.reviewed: Round 2. The full executed notebook of the first revision (commit 9e50d4b6e6), the helper module, the claims file and this record, with the paper. It agreed with 16 of the 17 outcomes and disagreed with fig4c-alpha-beta-shift; of its round-1 points it found 7 resolved and 3 (the PSI null, pairs treated as independent, the timing of the 1150-ms trials) partly resolved and bearing on a conclusion. It quoted six passages the outputs do not support.

disagreements.reason: The evidence does not support it. The partial match rests on the sign of subject means that are all close to zero, -1.35 to 0.46 (cell 48). Under reading (b) with the Methods' null, z is not centred on zero for independent signals; in a synthetic test (33 trials of independent 1/f and brown noise) reading (b) gave mean z of -0.32 to -0.34 in both bands, with SD 0.75 to 0.82 in delta-theta, and reading (a) a mean near 0 in delta-theta and -0.13 to -0.17 in alpha-beta, with SD about 1. An offset of that size alone would put most subjects below zero, and the data show the same pattern under (b). The record justifies reading (b) by its structure, not by calibration; the surrogate shows (b) is too conservative in delta-theta (SD 0.60, 0.1% pass rate) and in alpha-beta its per-subject rates run from 0% to 24%. If reading (a) were adopted, fig4c would be not reproduced, fig5b partial, and fig5a-spatiotemporal reproduced by the letter but uninformative. It asked for the surrogate's mean z per subject under (a) and (b), and possibly (b) with one permutation per trial.

entries.name: crcns-fcx-3-johnson-2019
entries.title: Frontoparietal working memory iEEG (Johnson et al. 2019) from CRCNS fcx-3
entries.description: Tests the findings of Johnson, King-Stephens, Weber, Laxer, Lin and Knight (2019) on CRCNS data set fcx-3, which holds intracranial recordings from prefrontal and parietal cortex of 7 patients doing a visuospatial working memory task. It checks the channel and trial counts, the behaviour, ERPs and power between identity, spatial and temporal trials with per-subject cluster tests, and the phase slope index between prefrontal and parietal channels over the delay and in time.
